evidence: On a grid too coarse for the powder-ring test, under one voxel across the widest FWHM it judges, fwhm_cap 0.16 Å⁻¹ (src/nebula3d/preprocessing/ring_isotropy.py:220, :231), the test judges no shell (ring_isotropy.py:280-283). The pooled ring removal confirms its rings with the same test (pooled_confirm_rings, on by default: src/nebula3d/pipeline.py:1079) and subtracts only the shells it confirms (src/nebula3d/preprocessing/pooled_rings.py:575-579), so on such a grid it subtracts none of the rings it detects, real powder rings included, and its log only counted them ("and N not judged (…; kept)", pipeline.py:1091-1098). Without the guard, the test judged a bump of the crystal's own at 1.75 Å⁻¹ a powder ring on the validation's dev crystal at n=81 (0.99 voxels across 0.16 Å⁻¹), which the removal would subtract. With it, on dev-rings at n=81 the removal detects three shells (2.18, 3.23 and 4.04 Å⁻¹, the planted rings at 2.2 and 4.05 Å⁻¹ among them), confirms none and subtracts none; at n=161 it confirms two and keeps one as the crystal's own.
proposed_fix: Accept that on a grid too coarse to confirm a ring the ring removal subtracts no unconfirmed ring, and say so out loud wherever the ring stage reports: its run log line and its diagnostics (GET /api/rings/{id}/diagnostics), the Execution page, the report's ring card and caveats, and the Pilot's ring check (assess_stage rings, notice; run_log): "N ring candidates (shells that may be powder rings or the crystal's own scattering) detected but not confirmed at this grid (needs ≥ <the limit, from the rule's constants>); not subtracted. Use a finer grid, or, from the Python API, set pooled_confirm_rings=False to subtract every candidate, the crystal's own shells included." (for one: "1 ring candidate (a shell that may be a powder ring or the crystal's own scattering) … to subtract it, even if it is the crystal's own shell."), its second sentence a remedy arm C reads without. No console setting for it. {{achieved}} says why the ring removal is not judged ("not judged: the ring removal (grid too coarse for the ring check)"), not that it was not measured.

evidence: The model-visible prompts stated criteria the verdicts no longer use. The system prompt said after_floor_max_sigma "≲ 1 is flat" (web/src/llm/prompts/system.ts:67), finding 6's 1σ clause, dropped on 2026-10-17: the flatten's verdict judges the pedestal alone (web/src/llm/verdicts/rules.ts:275; web/src/llm/metrics/flatten.ts:100), over the outer half of the |Q| shells the counts reach (flatten.ts:74), where the prompt took floor_trend "over the whole coverage" (system.ts:71). It said a back-FFT r "clearly below 1 flags a transform, crop or band problem" (system.ts:87-88), and the ΔPDF review asks whether the ΔPDF is "trustworthy (consistency_pearson_r)" (web/src/llm/prompts/templates.ts:86), while the verdict judges the round trip against the data's even part, back_fft_pearson_r_even, to 0.999 (rules.ts:295-297), and on unsymmetrised data r against the data is legitimately below 1; the flatten review asks for after_floor_max_sigma (templates.ts:85). The four checks (system.ts:130-135) covered the rings, the Bragg punch, the texture and Qmax, while {{achieved}} judges all five stages and the checks on their result and names the data's own problems (web/src/llm/verdicts/readers.ts:343, :353-390), so a reply that settled the four left it not judged. The ring check named the ring-energy ratio and the over-subtraction (system.ts:131-132), where the verdict reads max_ring_left and max_ring_dent at the confirmed rings; CRITERIA.flatten carried an internal note (rules.ts:268); "the context above" (system.ts:104) named context that arrives after the system prompt; and update_settings gives punchSearchMaxWidth as "number 1–6" with its default, 0 (off), outside it (web/src/llm/tools/index.ts:1556-1563; web/src/llm/tune/catalog.ts:233-238).
proposed_fix: Each sentence states what the verdict judges, in the verdict module's own words and limits (FLATTEN_FLOOR_SIGMA_NOTE, FLOOR_SIGMA_WHY, PEDESTAL_SHELLS, PEDESTAL_LIMIT, EVEN_PART, BACK_FFT_R_OK; the criteria built from the same constants), tagged by class: a criterion stated as what the verdict judges is a definition, read in both arms, and what a value is evidence of stays evidence. The four checks become six, the five stages as {{achieved}} names them (STAGE_NAMES), with the checks on their result, and the data's own problems (the UB, the HKL origin, the counts' edge); arm C reads the same properties as a plain, unordered list. The criterion's note goes, and the context is "in the first user message". punchSearchMaxWidth's range is written in a tool file and checked by the catalog's validator, which refuses 0: left for after the tools' refactor (#4).
